---
title: "Model building"
---

## Compose a model from Torch and Cellerator

Use PyTorch for ordinary tensors, standard layers, autograd, optimizers, and
training control. Add a Cellerator operation where the cellular model's
identity, relations, support, or repeated work changes the operation's
contract or execution. The intended model is a composition of these pieces;
Cellerator is not a second general-purpose deep-learning framework.

The current module surface is intentionally small. `Product2Module` is a real
`torch.nn.Module` with trainable coefficients, persistent indices, native
preparation, and first-order gradients. The optional CUDA `MechanismModule`
owns a specific native indexed-mechanism handle and lifecycle. Sparse support
modules model explicit ranked-gene and event-slice consumers. These components
have distinct backend, data, and maturity boundaries; they are not a uniform
layer stack. See [operations](operations.qmd) and the
[Python binding guide](development/python-bindings.md) for details.

## Keep scientific meaning with the model owner

Cellerator should expose reusable contracts without assigning biological
meaning to an input by convention. A scientific consumer defines how an entity,
relation, feature, event, or state is interpreted and validates that
interpretation. A numerical API should state the accepted identities, ordering,
value types, update behavior, and derivative contract without silently
inventing a domain ontology.

AnnData is required by the Python package and remains a standard interface in
the ecosystem. Current operations accept explicit arrays or tensors; there is
not yet a direct adapter that chooses AnnData layers, derives model structure,
or prepares a scientific model automatically. Classical data analysis and
preprocessing remain upstream in AnnData, Scanpy, or RAPIDS-singlecell.

## Parameters, state, and structure

Treat model structure, current activity, state values, and learned parameters
as separate things. A parameter update should not rebuild immutable structure
when an operation permits reuse, and a change of activity should have an
explicit support or invalidation path. A layout reorder must preserve the
mapping back to logical entities, outputs, and gradients. See
[layout and execution](layout_execution.qmd).

Use `torch.nn.Module` when it gives a useful owner for parameters, buffers,
composition, or checkpoint behavior. Otherwise a callable operation or native
API may be the better interface. New module types should follow from real
operations rather than a speculative catalog of biological layer names.

## Execution fields are experimental

The current `ExecutionField` composes a prepared Product2 module and makes
structure rebinding explicit. It is experimental, CPU FP32, and has no JIT or
live recompilation. Ordinary model use does not depend on an execution field.
The [experimental fields note](development/experimental-fields.md) documents
its exact boundary.
